# Licensed real-media fixtures

These two ordinary Git files are test inputs. They total 4,695,428 bytes (about 4.48 MiB). Tests never fetch them, and neither deterministic fixture checks nor required CI invokes recognition, diarization or model loading.

`speech.flac` is the exact 495,373-byte [Commons speech file](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Speech_12dB_s16.flac), credited to the IETF / OPUS Codec working group and a 16-bit lossless FLAC conversion by Commons contributor MüllerMarcus. Its license is [CC BY 3.0 Unported](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). This repository copies the source FLAC bytes without alteration. The file measures 10.8 seconds, mono, 48 kHz, 16-bit FLAC, 518,400 samples. Its source page revision and byte identity are pinned in `manifest.json`.

`sintel-dialogue.mkv` is a 30-second adaptation of *Sintel* (2010), by the Blender Foundation and contributors, distributed under [CC BY 3.0 Unported](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Required attribution: **(c) copyright Blender Foundation | durian.blender.org**. The [official sharing page](https://durian.blender.org/sharing/) permits adaptations with attribution. This excerpt uses the exact downloaded Commons 240p VP9/Opus rendition, rather than the full 4K original. It crops presentation timestamps 134 through 164 seconds, reencodes video as H.264 and converts all six 48 kHz audio channels to 16-bit FLAC. The input Opus audio was already lossy; the adaptation does not claim losslessness relative to the original film. Metadata/chapters are removed. The excerpt measures 30 seconds, 426 by 182 pixels and 1,440,000 samples per audio channel. The source rendition hash, page revision, measured streams and exact adaptation command/tool identity are in `manifest.json`.

The crop maps each local sample boundary to source ticks `6,432,000 + local_sample_index`, at 48,000 ticks per second. Thus the local origin is exactly source 134 seconds, without passing sample timing through millisecond video timestamps. Independently decoded source-crop and derived audio PCM bytes match exactly. Repeating the adaptation with the recorded FFmpeg binary also produces identical container bytes. The source rendition reported 48/1 frame rate despite 720 decoded frames per 30 seconds. The adaptation explicitly declares 24 fps, preserving those 720 frames; tests also check measured PCM/source-clock facts.

`speech-reference.json` cites an [independent upstream test](https://github.com/unslothai/unsloth/blob/971eb36f485d1d0de54f211ea12f6a985d18c173/tests/saving/text_to_speech_models/test_whisper.py#L190-L201) that downloads the same Commons file and asserts four distinctive Harvard phrases. The full phrase wording is corroborated by [Columbia's reproduced IEEE Appendix C](https://www.cs.columbia.edu/~hgs/audio/harvard.html), List 1 sentences 1, 2, 3 and 9. The speech SRT/VTT deliberately uses one whole-media cue: phrase-level timing and speaker count are unknown.

`sintel-reference.json` uses official English subtitle cues 8 through 12 from the [Blender subtitle publication](https://durian.blender.org/wp-content/content/subtitles/sintel_en.srt), with exactly 134,000 milliseconds subtracted. Their text and display times independently agree with the pinned [Commons English publication](https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?title=TimedText:Sintel_movie_4K.webm.en.srt&oldid=175198974&action=raw), after whitespace normalization. Character labels are editorial scene interpretation, supported by visually inspected frames, and are not biometric speaker identification.

Direct auditory input was unavailable during fixture preparation. Published subtitle display windows are not measured speech activity boundaries. Neither fixture asserts sample-accurate voice turns, and the speech sample does not assert an independently measured speaker count. `deterministic_turns` are explicit assembly-test adapter results, never generated recognition output or a second product assignment store. Actual elected engines can later be qualified independently outside CI; their results must not be filled from these references.

The adjacent SRT/VTT files are supplied test oracles, with original text and deliberate display windows. Their references, byte digests and lengths are pinned. The manifests carry license attribution separately from the repository's Apache-2.0 code license. The fixture media and derived film subtitles remain CC BY 3.0.

Run the offline integrity suite with `python scripts/test-media-fixtures.py`. After exact native tools have been prepared, run `python scripts/media-fixtures.py --native` for bounded probe/decode and stream/channel checks. The receipt records tool identities, full PCM hashes and mapped sample counts, and explicitly states that inference was not invoked. Required checks must not add recognition/diarization imports, model initialization or weight downloads to this path.
